author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected under the same rules as booking; the correction changes that visit in place, never adds another, and is reached by its page address alone.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit is opened, then the existing visit form (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) renders with its `visit` model attribute prefilled with that visit's current date and description

given a booked visit, when a non-blank description and a date later than today are POSTed to the same URL, then that visit is updated in place, the pet's visit count is unchanged, and the response redirects to the owner detail page
given a blank description, when the correction is POSTed, then it is refused with a field error on description and the visit form is redisplayed
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is POSTed, then it is refused with a field error on date and the visit form is redisplayed
given a visitId that does not belong to the named pet, when the correction is opened or POSTed, then it is refused and no visit changes (PRD Visits edge case 3)
non_goals: cancelling or deleting a booked visit (NG-5 narrowed, NG-4 unchanged)
an edit link or any visible entry point on the owner detail page (owner decision: reachable by URL alone; possible follow-up)
a new confirmation message on successful correction (would add wording to every supported language; not requested)
relaxing the future-date rule for corrections of past visits
notes: Owner absent; narrowest readings taken per the intake. Open points recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: (1) visible entry point on the owner record is a possible follow-up; (2) the future-date rule means a correction cannot keep a past visit's own date. Edge case 3 (visit not belonging to the named pet is refused) is my craft reading of 'updates that visit in place'; refusal form (404-style error page vs form error) is left to system-design-expert. NG-5 narrowing recorded in new non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-11-05-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md; the 2026-08-08 ADR status line now points to it. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new ADR; it is outside my write scope. No prd-autofix records to audit.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is a second flow on the existing VisitController over the existing owner aggregate (system-design.md § Contracts invariants paragraph: Pet and Visit persist only by cascade from Owner; OwnerRepository is the sole write path). No new type, package, or pattern. Adjustments recorded in docs/system-design.md: (1) Pet resolves one of its own visits by identity (aggregate navigation through the root, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer)); (2) the non-future-date check stays the single recorded controller rule and serves both booking and correction from one place in VisitController, never a second copy; (3) VisitController's binder admits only the visit form's fields (date, description) while still disallowing id and *.id; (4) a new § Scale and Load section with the visit-correction lookup row. The verdict is minor, not covered, because the shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader today creates a new Visit and adds it to the pet on every request: reused unchanged on the edit routes it would add a phantom visit and break the in-place guarantee. The loader must resolve the existing visit when a visitId path variable is present and create the new one only when it is absent. Basis for the code claims: grep and file reads of VisitController.java, Pet.java, Owner.java, Visit.java, createOrUpdateVisitForm.html (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis). Template needs no change: the form has no th:action so it posts back to the edit URL, the heading already drops 'New' for a persisted visit, and the previous-visits table lists the pet's visits.
integration_points: GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit on VisitController, rendering pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm with the `visit` model attribute; success redirects to /owners/{ownerId}

Model-attribute resolution: owner by OwnerRepository.findById, pet by Owner.getPet(Integer), visit by the new Pet lookup by identity; an unknown owner, pet, or visit-not-of-this-pet is refused the way the booking flow refuses an unknown pet today (IllegalArgumentException from the resolver, rendered by the error page) before any binding or save (PRD Visits edge case 3)

Binding target for the new POST entry point: the persisted Visit resolved through the owner aggregate, behind an allow-list of date and description on the controller binder, with id and *.id still disallowed (security-principles.md § Language Realization, Mass assignment row). Owner is never a binding target: the existing booking handler's @ModelAttribute Owner binds request parameters onto the owner, and the correction handler must not copy that; the binder allow-list closes it for both handlers

Write: the resolved visit is mutated by binding and the owner is saved through OwnerRepository.save; no Owner.addVisit or Pet.addVisit call on this path, so the pet's visit count is unchanged. On a validation failure no save happens; open-in-view is off, so the detached graph is not flushed

Doubles: the framework transport is MockMvc (the sanctioned mock). The repository boundary uses the existing class fixture's @MockitoBean OwnerRepository, a conscious framework-stub exception: the @WebMvcTest slice needs an OwnerRepository bean and a hand-written double would implement the whole JpaRepository surface. New tests reuse that fixture, add a persisted visit with a set id to the fixture pet, assert the in-place change on the fixture object, and use verify(owners, never()).save(any()) for refusals

patterns.description: Owner.getPet(Integer) — identity lookup through the root; the Pet visit lookup mirrors it
create and edit flows sharing one controller and one form template, keyed on the entity's isNew()
existing non-future-date rejection (field 'date', code typeMismatch.visitDate); extract it once and call it from both POST handlers

risks.risk: The shared @ModelAttribute("visit") loader adds a new Visit to the pet on every request, including the edit routes
risks.mitigation: Branch the loader on the optional visitId path variable: resolve the existing visit when present, create and attach a new one only when absent (system-design.md § Contracts invariants: a visit is corrected in place)

risks.risk: Duplicating the non-future-date check in the correction handler would be a fresh business rule in a controller
risks.mitigation: One shared check serves both handlers (architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row and its deviation note; system-design.md VisitController row)

risks.risk: Visit-correction lookup scans the pet's visits
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form, a linear scan; system-design.md § Scale and Load, visit-correction lookup row

risks.risk: The allow-list on the shared binder also changes the booking route: request parameters other than date and description no longer bind onto Visit or Owner there
risks.mitigation: Restriction only; legitimate booking submissions carry date and description, and existing booking tests must stay green (security-principles.md § Language Realization, Mass assignment row)

risks.risk: Refusal messages reach the error page, which renders exception text (system-design.md Known Defects, error page row)
risks.mitigation: The refusal message carries only the path identifiers, like the existing pet refusal; no other value (security-principles.md § Language Realization, Secret disclosure row)

risks.risk: Two concurrent corrections of one visit: the last save wins with no version check
risks.mitigation: Accepted at the demonstration's baseline; every other edit flow has the same property and the PRD names no concurrency requirement

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. ADR index: added the 2026-11-05 non-goal ADR row to docs/adr/README.md and marked the 2026-08-08 row's NG-5 narrowing, as the product expert requested. No architectural ADR: every choice here is contained in this slice. Owner absent; narrowest readings taken, open points for the owner: (1) the submit button keeps the 'Add Visit' label on a correction, since a new 'Update Visit' key would add wording to all eleven locales (REQ-LANG-002) and the PRD declines new wording; proposed follow-up sentence: 'The visit form's button reads Update Visit when correcting a booked visit.' (2) A successful correction redirects without a flash message; the booking flow's 'Your visit has been booked' text would misstate a correction, and a new message is a PRD non-goal. (3) Edge case 3's refusal uses the existing error-page form for unresolvable path identifiers, not a form error. (4) The binder allow-list incidentally closes a latent gap where the booking POST binds request parameters onto Owner; flagged for the security reviewer.

findings.description: docs/system-design.md assigns Pet the rule 'resolves one of its own visits by identity' (Contracts row `Pet`) and its Scale and Load row for 'Visit correction lookup' names a linear scan, so Pet.getVisit(int) is a domain seam below the web boundary. findings.fix: Add a unit test class for Pet (e.g. PetTests, plain objects, no Spring) with named tests for getVisit: finds the visit by id among several, is empty for a pet with no visits, is empty for an id that belongs to another pet's visit. findings.description: The correction POST never submits an `id` field. The binder change adds setAllowedFields("date","description") and keeps setDisallowedFields("id","*.id"), and system-design.md's threat-model row cites identifier tampering on the visit routes. approved_aspects: Mass assignment (security-principles.md row): VisitController.java:55 `dataBinder.setAllowedFields("date", "description");` adds an allow-list on top of the retained `setDisallowedFields("id", "*.id")`; because @InitBinder without a name applies to every attribute this controller binds, it also stops the pre-existing booking POST from binding Owner fields (firstName, address, etc.) onto the `@ModelAttribute Owner` it saves, so the change strengthens the baseline rather than weakening it

Identifier tampering / IDOR within the owner aggregate: the visit is resolved by `pet.getVisit(visitId)` (Pet.java new method filtering `getVisits()` by id) on a pet resolved via `owner.getPet(petId)` from the path owner (VisitController.java:72), so a visit id from another pet is refused with IllegalArgumentException before binding; each request re-resolves owner, pet, and visit from the path (trusting-cross-request-state row satisfied); the cross-pet refusal is covered by theVisitCorrectionShouldRefuseAVisitThatDoesNotBelongToThePet
